ai.description: *Raorchestes archeos* is a small shrub frog (18–20 mm) with a brown dorsum and distinct dark interorbital markings. It features granular skin and lacks a vocal sac.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes archeos* is best distinguished by its unique, distinctively granular skin texture and the presence of a prominent, dark-pigmented "X" or hourglass marking on its back.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes archeos* inhabits the high-altitude montane evergreen forests (shola) of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Raorchestes archeos* is primarily nocturnal, remaining active during the night to forage for small invertebrates among the leaf litter and low vegetation of its habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes archeos* undergoes direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. Breeding occurs during the monsoon, with females laying small clutches of terrestrial eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes archeos* is endemic to the high-elevation shola-grassland mosaics of the Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically found above 1,800 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes archeos* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation in high-altitude forests.
